text: Researchers filmed doctors in training with their patients... and measured which doctors felt like frauds.
A researcher at M I T asked each young doctor how often they had impostor thoughts... the feeling that you're not as good as people think.
Then the patients rated them. The doctors with more impostor thoughts came out as more empathetic... and better listeners.
On video, they made more eye contact and nodded more. Feeling unsure made them focus on the patient.
But don't wish for the feeling. It also lowered self esteem. The real lesson? Feeling like a fraud is not evidence that you are one.
So next time that voice says they'll find out... maybe what they'll find is someone who listens.
Where does the impostor feeling hit you most? School, work, or somewhere else?
